evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: A vulnerability was discovered in the PyYAML library in versions before 5.4, where it is susceptible to arbitrary code execution when it processes untrusted YAML files through the full_load method or with the FullLoader loader. Applications that use the library to process untrusted input may be vulnerable to this flaw. This flaw allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system by abusing the python/object/new constructor. This flaw is due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2020-1747.

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-15 to comply with the real-service + external-HTTP policy (the prior build triggered yaml.full_load in-process via a stdin driver -- BANNED). Now: each profile pip-installs the EXACT published PyYAML sdist (5.3/5.3.1/5.4) on python:3.8-slim and stands up a REAL minimal Flask service (app.py) whose `POST /parse` runs the REAL, unmodified `data = yaml.full_load(request.data)` over the raw attacker-supplied request body -- exactly how an app that parses user-supplied YAML (config upload, API body) behaves. The trigger is EXTERNAL HTTP: the oracle/PoCs run on the HOST and POST the YAML to the version's published port (v0=34810/v1=34811/v2=34812); the flag is only obtainable through the real full_load object escape. Canary planted in the environment via the compose command wrapper (/flag from $PCB_FLAG). Gate run via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`; see repro.log (flag PCBFLAG_ea55f3895fb1c54fafb77d790e4e2e06). Sink = yaml.full_load -> FullConstructor python/object/new. The FullConstructor python/object* table is IDENTICAL in 5.3 and 5.3.1; the CVE-2020-1747 fix (5.3.1) only added a STATE-key blacklist (get_state_keys_blacklist=['^extend$','^__.*__$'] + check_state_key). ORIGINAL poisons `extend` via `state:` on an _frozen_importlib.ModuleSpec instance (writable __dict__, no __setstate__ so check_state_key fires): flag in /parse response on 5.3 (loaded), blocked on 5.3.1 (ConstructorError: blacklisted key 'extend' in instance state found). RESIDUAL moves the poisoned `extend` into the class-CONSTRUCTION map via python/object/new:type + a python/tuple bases + a namespace map {extend: exec} -- the state blacklist never inspects construction args -- flag in /parse response on 5.3.1 (loaded), blocked on 5.4 (ConstructorError: could not determine a constructor for python/object/new:type, because a001f27 MOVED python/module|object|object/new|object/apply to UnsafeConstructor). Benign read-exfil only: the invoked `extend`=exec runs a local file read+copy of /flag into /out/leak.txt; no shell, no subprocess, no network, no persistence, no PyYAML modification.
